pool.text: Dutch colonists built Fort Nassau on the Delaware River in what is now New Jersey.
Swedish settlers established the colony of New Sweden at Fort Christina in Delaware.
William Penn founded Philadelphia as capital of the colonial era Province of Pennsylvania.
Benjamin Franklin established the Library Company of Philadelphia at Locust Street.
Philadelphia hosted the First Continental Congress at Carpenters Hall with twelve colonies.
Philadelphia began sourcing its water via the Fairmount Water Works on the Schuylkill River.
The PSFS Building became the first modern International Style skyscraper.
Independence Day celebration of the Declaration was officially formalized.
Southeastern Pennsylvania was assigned the 215 area code.
The population peaked at more than two million residents before declining.
The teen dance party program called Bandstand premiered on local television.
The Philadelphia Historical Commission was created to preserve cultural history.
Lobbying helped create the Percent for Art ordinance for public art.
Geno's Steaks was founded across the intersection in South Philadelphia.
The City Tavern was rebuilt on the same site as part of the park.
The police department bombed the Cobbs Creek neighborhood to execute warrants.
One Liberty Place was completed and surpassed City Hall in height.
Navy operations at the Philadelphia Naval Shipyard finally ended.
SEPTA reintroduced trolley service to the Girard Avenue Line, Route 15.
Philadelphia's homicide rate was the highest of the country's populous cities.
